findings.title: Targets are interpolated twice on the sharded path
findings.body: runShardSplitQuery now calls applyTemplateVariables on every target, and the resulting targets are passed into splitQueriesByStreamShard, which builds subRequest and calls runSplitQuery(datasource, subRequest, ...). runSplitQuery in querySplitting.ts (line 299 in the head) now also calls applyTemplateVariables on each target, with the same scopedVars and filters. Every sharded sub-request is therefore interpolated a second time. Any value that survives the first pass but is changed by a second pass (a value containing '$', regex-escaped label values, or adhoc filters applied again) gets corrupted or duplicated. The fix is to interpolate in exactly one layer, or to skip interpolation in runSplitQuery when the caller has already done it.

findings.title: runSplitQuery interpolates unconditionally, including for callers that already interpolated
findings.body: The map to applyTemplateVariables was added to runSplitQuery, which is a public entry point. Besides shardQuerySplitting (see the double-interpolation finding), any other caller that passes already-interpolated targets now gets them interpolated again. There is no flag or contract documenting which layer owns interpolation, so the behaviour depends on the call path.

findings.title: Call-count assertion hard-codes an implementation detail
findings.body: The 'Interpolates queries before running' test now asserts applyTemplateVariables was called exactly 5 times. That count only holds because of the nested runSplitQuery re-interpolation, so the test encodes the double-interpolation behaviour as expected and would not catch a regression in either direction. It should assert what the sharded path must do (interpolate each original target once) rather than an incidental call count.
